alignments.note: Improper preposition rendered by a single English word; that word is the head, rule 71.
Supplied *a* on the anarthrous governed noun, rule 51.
Ordinary negative, discontinuous from its verb under rule 15.
Inverted subject rides with the verb.
Case preposition rides with the dative pronoun.

κατ᾽ ἰδίαν rendered by the single word *privately*, which answers to neither token separately (rule 45); headed on the governed word. Joined rather than split: rule 93 decides the rule 34/45 divide from what the corpus spends on the governed word, and it spends an *own* word on ἴδιος in 54 of that lemma's 69 units and *private* once attributively at 2PE.1.20, but never *privately* for the bare adjective — so the preposition is inside the English word and rule 34's pleonastic case does not reach it. The corpus carries the phrase undivided in all nine of its units: `noncompositional` at GAL.2.2, MRK.7.33 and MRK.9.28, and → *apart* at LUK.9.10, MRK.6.31, MRK.6.32 and MRK.9.2. Reading it `aligned` on the ground that *private-* visibly carries the ἰδι- lexeme is the competing analysis and stands at LUK.10.23 and MAT.24.3; Mark's own five units are all `noncompositional`, so this follows them.
Article emptied by the possessive adjective ἴδιος, which carries *his own*, rule 47.
ἴδιος carries the supplied possessive, rule 47.
Case preposition rides with the noun, the article having no determiner to anchor; discontinuous under rule 15.
Supplied subject rides with the verb; head on the lexical verb.
Anarthrous substantival adjective with the generic *things*; head on the adjective, rule 17.

review_notes: Corrected: κατ᾽ ἰδίαν (s007, s008) is now one `noncompositional` unit on *privately* (t011), headed on the governed word. The verse pass left κατ `unrepresented` under rules 34 and 93; that turned on *privately* being the ordinary gloss of ἴδιος, and it is not.

The precedent is nine corpus units of the phrase, none split, five of them in Mark: *apart* at MRK.6.31, MRK.6.32, MRK.9.2 and LUK.9.10, *privately* at MRK.7.33, MRK.9.28 and GAL.2.2 (`noncompositional`) and at LUK.10.23 and MAT.24.3 (`aligned`).
MRK.4.10's κατὰ μόνας → *alone* is deliberately not changed with this: `μόνος` takes *alone* in sixteen corpus units, so rule 34 splits it there. The chapter's convention log records the divide.

No other unit in the verse changes. τοῖς (s010) stays `unrepresented` under rule 47 despite the BSB disagreement, and the unit count falls from 14 to 13 with all fourteen source ids and all nineteen target ids still partitioned exactly once.
